items.title: The impossible standard we're setting for artificial intelligence | The Jerusalem Post
items.summary:
Artificial intelligence.

Artificial intelligence. (credit: SHUTTERSTOCK)

Others fear that increasingly autonomous AI will eventually become impossible to control. These concerns deserve serious attention, particularly as AI agents gain access to financial systems, corporate networks, sensitive information, and critical infrastructure. [...] Until recently, AI was largely an assistant; we asked it questions, evaluated its responses, and decided what to do with the information. Increasingly, we are asking AI to carry out the work directly.

An agent can be given an objective, determine the steps required, and execute them with limited human involvement. This transition has understandably generated anxiety as people worry about losing their jobs to systems that can perform tasks faster and more cheaply than they can. [...] Updated:

Four years ago, most people had never held a conversation with an AI system. Today, millions routinely turn to ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini for everything from writing software to making financial decisions.

In that short period, we have witnessed a remarkable technological transformation, and I believe the most consequential stage is only beginning. The emergence of autonomous AI agents represents a fundamental change in our relationship with machines.

items.title: The U.S.–China AI Competition: Two Paths to Artificial General Intelligence | Center for Security and Emerging Technology
items.summary:
AGI has no universally accepted technical definition. In the U.S. frontier-model ecosystem, discussions commonly center on whether a system can reason, learn, and perform a wide range of tasks at broadly human levels—AGI—or substantially exceed human capabilities across those tasks—artificial superintelligence (ASI). This outlook encourages investment in larger and more capable models, advanced reasoning, and agents that can carry out extended sequences of work. [...] Recent op-eds comparing the United States’ and China’s artificial intelligence (AI) programs fault the former for its focus on artificial general intelligence (AGI) while praising China for its success in applying AI throughout the whole… Read More

Reports #### Chinese Critiques of Large Language Models January 2025 [...] U.S. developers define AGI in terms of broadly human-level intellectual capabilities across a wide range of cognitive tasks. China’s discourse on “general AI” places greater weight on the extension of intelligent capabilities to physical and social systems.

items.title: Howard Professor Danda B. Rawat Receives $700,000 NSF Award for AI Research | The Dig at Howard University
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to support decision-making in areas critical to public infrastructure, such as transportation, emergency response, and national security. While today's AI technologies can analyze vast amounts of data, many produce results without clearly explaining how decisions are made. The three-year project, led by Rawat, will develop innovative technologies for artificial general intelligence (AGI) capabilities. Rawat also serves as associate dean of [...] Danda B. Rawat, Ph.D., a professor of computer science in Howard University’s College of Engineering and Architecture, and the director of the AI Center of Excellence (AICoE), has received a $700,000 award from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to conduct research focused on one of the most pressing challenges in artificial intelligence: how to build AI systems that people can trust. [...] “As AI advances towards AGI and becomes increasingly integral to our lives, workplaces, and national defense, developing AI systems that people can trust, whether as teammates, leaders, or assistants, is more important than ever. We will leverage neuro-symbolic AI for advanced scene understanding in critical applications, enabling AI to reason, adapt, and collaborate safely and effectively with humans,” Rawat said.

items.title: Sở Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Tĩnh hướng dẫn xét công nhận sáng kiến và đánh giá hiệu quả đề tài khoa học
items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật [...] Đối với các đề tài khoa học, đề án khoa học và công trình khoa học – công nghệ, việc xét nghiệm thu thực hiện theo quy định của pháp luật về khoa học và công nghệ. Các đề tài chỉ được xem xét công nhận hiệu quả áp dụng và phạm vi ảnh hưởng khi đã được nghiệm thu đạt yêu cầu trở lên.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của $x^2$ (tích phân bất định $\int x^2 \, dx$) là:

$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

*(Trong đó $C$ là hằng số thực bất kỳ).*

**Công thức áp dụng:**
Công thức nguyên hàm lũy thừa tổng quát:
$$\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \quad (với \ n \neq -1)$$

Với $n = 2$, ta có:
$$\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C$$

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là một hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.

    Lưu ý: Cách này có độ phức tạp thời gian O(2^n) nên chỉ phù hợp với các số n
    nhỏ (n <= 30).
    """
    # Điều kiện cơ sở (base cases)
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1

    # Bước đệ quy
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)


# Ví dụ sử dụng:
# In ra 10 số Fibonacci đầu tiên
for i in range(10):
    print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

### Lưu ý quan trọng khi dùng đệ quy cho Fibonacci:
1. **Hiệu suất thấp:** Cách đệ quy thuần túy này tính toán lặp lại rất nhiều lần các giá trị đã tính (ví dụ: `fibonacci(n-2)` bị tính trùng ở cả nhánh `fibonacci(n-1)` và `fibonacci(n-2)`). Độ phức tạp là $O(2^n)$.
2. **Khắc phục:** Nếu bạn cần tính với `n` lớn hơn (ví dụ $n > 30$), bạn nên dùng:
   - **Memoization** (ghi nhớ kết quả đã tính bằng `@functools.lru_cache`).
   - Hoặc dùng **vòng lặp (iteration)** để đạt độ phức tạp $O(n)$.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
